Yes, you can use this track while stretching if it feels good for you. For calmer stretching or recovery, I would usually recommend something closer to the alpha range, around 10 Hz. These are the sessions with the green brain visuals on the channel.

For workouts, this track can also work, especially if it helps you feel more motivated and engaged. But for very intense training, you may prefer a more energizing high-beta or gamma session, but it also depends on your personal taste and how it feels for you. Thank you for listening.

Bei einem Freund von mir wirkt es nicht. Woran kann das liegen?!

Das kann mehrere Erklärungen haben. Die wissenschaftliche Forschung zeigt, dass auditive Beats ein messbares Entrainment der Gehirnwellen auslösen. Aber die wahrgenommene Wirkung unterscheidet sich von Person zu Person. Bei deinem Freund müsste die Monaural-Beat-Ebene vielleicht etwas deutlicher hörbar sein, oder sein aktueller Müdigkeits-, Stress- oder Konzentrationszustand spielt eine Rolle. Und selbst wenn er keinen klaren Effekt spürt, kann er die Musik natürlich trotzdem einfach als Fokusmusik genießen :). Schließlich kann es auch an der Ausrüstung liegen, über die er die Musik hört.

Try time blocking. Don't make a check list or to-do  list for your day. instead write your activities when  you want to do them. Here's two tips you must follow if it is to work. 1) move your phone or other distraction away from you. 2)stop when time is up, even if you spent half the block doodling or day dreaming, and write the same activity in for the next day. you have to sustain this to train your brain to start thinking faster on task. and since you stop and move on to next thing once time is up you are sending a signal to your brain that it has limited time. Block in 'free' time and try this for 2 weeks at least to see what happens. I used to procrastinate also. Oh, and it helps in general if you have long term plans and goals and then connect your productivity now to your future success.

Try time blocking. Don't make a check list or to-do  list for your day. instead write your activities when  you want to do them. Here's two tips you must follow if it is to work. 1) move your phone or other distraction away from you. 2)stop when time is up, even if you spent half the block doodling or day dreaming, and write the same activity in for the next day. you have to sustain this to train your brain to start thinking faster on task. and since you stop and move on to next thing once time is up you are sending a signal to your brain that it has limited time. Block in 'free' time and try this for 2 weeks at least to see what happens. I used to procrastinate also. Oh, and it helps in general if you have long term plans and goals and then connect your productivity now to your future success.
